answers: lens-correctness-design finding 1: wrong — The design fully and explicitly addresses this scenario. Gap 11 in the Context/gaps section names the exact problem the finding raises: in combined `--resume --from-stage <s>` mode, once the target unit is found and `skip_until_stage` is cleared, `resume_mode` remains `true`, which causes the resume skip guard (`$resume_mode && [[ -z "$skip_until_stage" ]]`) to activate for all subsequent units marked complete — silently skipping stages the user intends to run. The Decision paragraph contains the required fix: in both dispatch-unit arms (cycle:\* and stage:\*) of `main()` in runner.sh, immediately after clearing `skip_until_stage`, also set `resume_mode=false` — preventing the skip guard from firing for any unit after `<s>`; pure resume runs never set `skip_until_stage` so this path is unreachable for them. DSFSTG-3[code] provides the observable test that pins this: a 3-unit fixture `[intake, cyc, verify]` with all three marked complete, invoked with `--resume --from-stage cyc`, must emit stage.start for `verify` — the test fails on old code (verify is skipped) and passes after the fix. This is documented as Gap 11, Findings 30 and 31, and the DSFSTG-3 SPEC in the design. No design change is required.
